artifacts.summary: Gap analysis: the typescript extension's 20-file manifest, python-parity shape, and the 4 python-lacks items (hard_contracts, keyword_overrides, rules file, verification hook) already exist and are fully committed from task 620. All relevant lints re-run clean. The one genuinely open item -- the dispatch's own deploy-and-confirm VERIFICATION clause -- was executed directly against a disposable scratch repo and passed: .claude/ files, merged CLAUDE.md section, merged index.json entries, and (once an opencode.json.managed marker was added) the merged opencode.json agent keys.

memory_candidates.content: To headlessly load a new/unloaded agent-system extension into a scratch target repo for end-to-end merge-target verification, run nvim --headless with a lua one-liner calling manager.load('core', {confirm=false, force=true, project_dir=SCRATCH}) then manager.load('<ext>', {confirm=false, force=true, project_dir=SCRATCH}) (same pattern deploy-headless.sh uses internally for its bootstrap call). Afterward inspect SCRATCH/.claude/** for provided files, SCRATCH/.claude/CLAUDE.md for the merged section_id block, and SCRATCH/.claude/context/index.json for merged index entries.

merge.lua's generate_opencode_json() gates all output behind a target_path .. '.managed' marker file (opencode.json.managed) in the project root -- absent that marker it returns ok=true, err=nil but writes nothing, which looks like silent success rather than a no-op. Testing an extension's opencode_json merge target end-to-end against a fresh/scratch repo requires creating that marker file first.
